# Part IV: Integration, Verification, and Deployment {.unnumbered}

You have architected the machine. Its mechanical body respects physical limits, its training pipelines generate robust continuous policies, its runtime stack processes sensory observations at multi-rate cadences, and its silicon boundaries are isolated. Part IV covers the systems engineering required to integrate, stress-test, qualify, ship, and operate physical AI systems in the real world.

Deploying a physical AI system into an open, changing physical environment requires rigorous systems discipline: managing shared human-robot authority, qualifying hardware across simulation and physical benches, automating release decisions, and managing field operations.

### The Pillars of Part IV

Part IV guides the machine through systems integration, qualification, and field deployment:

* **Chapter 14: Shared Autonomy & Human Intervention (*Supervisory Control & Teleoperation*):** Integrates human operators alongside autonomous policies, formalizing bumpless control authority transfer, network-delayed teleoperation limits ($T_{\text{RTT}} \le 70\text{ ms}$), and immutable telemetry auditing.
* **Chapter 15: Hardware-in-the-Loop Verification (*Synthetic Fault Injection & Stress Testing*):** Establishes the 4-stage qualification ladder ($\text{Simulation} \to \text{Processor-in-the-Loop} \to \text{Hardware-in-the-Loop} \to \text{In-Situ}$), injecting sensor dropout, bus starvation, power rail droop, and temporal logic stress tests on physical testbeds.
* **Chapter 16: System Release & Production Operations (*Assurance Cases, Telemetry & OTA Updates*):** Formalizes release engineering via structured Claim-Argument-Evidence trees, defines evidence-backed release verdicts (*Operate*, *Operate with Conditions*, *Refuse Deployment*), and establishes over-the-air firmware update mechanisms.
* **Chapter 17: The Frontier of Physical AI (*Open Systems Challenges & Horizons*):** Concludes the text by analyzing the fundamental frontier challenges in embodied AI: end-to-end foundation models versus modular systems architectures, self-improving robots, and open physical limits.

### What You Will Master in Part IV

By the conclusion of Part IV, you will possess the practical systems expertise to build, qualify, and operate physical AI machines in production:

1. **Bumpless Authority Transfer:** Designing supervisory interfaces and shared autonomy blending that eliminate mode confusion and operator latency traps.
2. **HIL Bench Instrumentation:** Rigorously stress-testing physical AI machines against real hardware faults using synchronized testbed oscilloscopes, motor dynos, and synthetic fault injectors.
3. **Evidence-Backed Release:** Grounding deployment decisions in measurable empirical data, clear operational envelopes, and fleet monitoring telemetry.
